title: Best Cabin-Approved Strollers UK
short: Seven strollers built to fold small enough for the overhead locker, tested by parents on real flights and airport trips.
intro: To count as cabin-approved, a stroller must fold within IATA's carry-on dimensions (56 x 45 x 25cm) and weigh under 10kg, so it can go in the overhead locker instead of the hold, though it's worth double-checking with your airline before flying. This guide is based on Mumsnet's tested roundup (updated July 2026), built on forum recommendations, Which? lab data and parent-testers who used each stroller on real journeys, including actual flights. It covers models not already featured in our separate lightweight strollers guide (such as the Stokke YOYO³, iCandy Pip, Cybex Orfeo, Joolz Aer² and Cybex Libelle, all also cabin-approved). Prices shown are RRPs quoted by Mumsnet.

products.name: Pact
products.best_for: A feature-rich, affordable stroller for holidays
products.key_spec: Birth to 3 years/15kg, 6kg, one-handed unfold in 6 seconds, lie-flat position, storage large enough for a backpack
products.summary: Mumsnet found the Joie Pact balances affordability with functionality: lightweight for agility in tight spaces, with a custom carry strap and bag, an all-weather UPF50+ canopy, and locking swivel wheels with four-wheel suspension for a smooth ride on bumpy surfaces. It doesn't fold completely flat and can feel a little clumsy to carry without the bag, and the small footrest means taller children's legs may dangle.
pros: Storage basket large enough for a backpack
cons: The seat maintains a notable angle even upright

products.name: Pisces
products.best_for: Babies and younger toddlers on holiday, at the lowest price for a cabin-approved stroller
products.key_spec: Birth to 4 years, 4.9kg, rain cover included, UPF50+ extendable hood, peekaboo window
products.summary: Mumsnet's editor Laura called it the lightest stroller she's ever tested, making a huge difference lifting it in and out of a car or up plane steps. Tester Nicola used it on a family holiday to Cyprus and found it fitted into overhead lockers on both flights, meaning no waiting at baggage claim. It's not quite as refined as pricier travel strollers like the Stokke YOYO³ or Bugaboo Butterfly 2: it needs two hands to fold, has no shoulder strap or carry bag, and older preschoolers may outgrow the seat before the 22kg limit.
pros: Easy to steer around airports and resorts
cons: Two-handed fold can be awkward juggling luggage and a child
Small storage basket, no shoulder strap or carry bag
Seat suits babies and younger toddlers best

products.name: Jet 5
products.best_for: Parents who want to pull the folded stroller like a mini suitcase through the airport
products.key_spec: Birth to about 22kg, 7.5kg, magnetic buckle system, one-motion fold, lie-flat recline, dust and rain cover included
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Michaela found a sleek upgrade on the Jet 3 with a wider, plusher seat, a faster fold and a magnetic buckle system unique among compact strollers, unlocking and folding flat in seconds. It has a full lie-flat recline for newborns, an extra-large UPF50+ canopy with a flip-out visor, and good ventilation via a magnetic back flap and peekaboo window. The storage basket is small, holding only up to 5kg and accessible from the front only.
pros: Can be pulled along like a mini suitcase
Comes with a dust cover and rain cover
cons: Some say it's a little flimsy with heavy bags hung on it
Small storage basket, accessible from the front only

products.name: Butterfly 2
products.best_for: Parents who want a roomy, genuinely from-birth compact stroller
products.key_spec: Birth to about 4 years, 7.3kg, lie-flat recline, washable seat covers, compatible with Cybex, Britax and BeSafe car seats
products.summary: Mumsnet's editor Laura was impressed by its intuitive fold, high-quality fabrics and generous 8kg storage basket that outperforms many competitors. A newly fully lie-flat recline means it's now suitable from birth, not just six months, and despite its compact frame it feels really roomy, especially for toddlers with longer legs. The frame now uses bio-based and recycled materials, cutting CO₂ by 37% versus the original. The handlebar isn't height adjustable, no bumper bar is included, and the carry strap is a little short for taller people.
pros: Super lightweight and compact, folds with two buttons
cons: Carry strap is a little short for taller people

products.name: Yo! Stroller
products.best_for: Parents who want a fun, design-led stroller with a long warranty
products.key_spec: Birth to 25kg, 7kg, IATA compliant, one-handed fold, 8kg storage basket, 4-year warranty
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Rachel said the sturdy compact frame, combined with Cosatto's four-year guarantee, makes it one of the most reliable and indispensable cabin-approved strollers on the market. It comes in four eye-catching designs with eco-friendly fabrics and a vegan leather handlebar, fully reclines, and has a large storage basket. The sun canopy could offer more coverage on bright days, the rain cover fits too snugly, it's world-facing only, and it isn't travel system compatible.
pros: Weighs just 7kg and is IATA compliant
cons: Instruction manual not easy to follow

products.name: Minu V3
products.best_for: Daily use in a busy town as well as travel, with no assembly required
products.key_spec: Birth (with newborn pack) to 4 years, 7.5kg, 45.7cm wide, no assembly, large sun canopy
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Tina used it nearly every day in a busy town environment: bumped up and down kerbs on the school run, wheeled to swimming lessons and parks, folded into tight car boots, and taken on trains where its compact fold and light weight came into their own. At just 45.7cm wide it's easy to manoeuvre through narrow shop aisles and onto public transport, and it fits most airline overhead lockers. It's pricey, the handlebar isn't adjustable, and it isn't suited to all terrain.
pros: Spacious storage basket and large sun canopy

products.name: Lara²
products.best_for: Sturdy performance on cobbles and uneven pavements without paying a premium
products.key_spec: Birth to 4 years, 6.4kg, IATA-approved fold, two storage baskets, five-point harness
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Charlotte, testing it on a family trip to Italy, was pleasantly surprised how sturdy it felt on public transport and over cobbled streets, gravel paths and uneven pavements, conditions that expose weaknesses in cheaper travel strollers. At under £200 it offers strong value, with EVA puncture-proof wheels, two storage baskets and a large sun canopy. The padded handlebar is comfortable but not adjustable, it doesn't lie flat, and the harness clasp buttons are stiff and can't be operated one-handed.
pros: Lightweight at 6.4kg, easy to carry and store
Easy to push and steer, five-point harness

guide.q: What actually makes a stroller cabin-approved?
guide.a: It must fold to within IATA's carry-on dimensions of 56 x 45 x 25cm and weigh under 10kg. All the strollers here meet that, but airline rules can still vary, so check with your specific airline before flying, especially on budget carriers with smaller overhead lockers.

guide.q: Which is best for a newborn?
guide.a: Look for a full lie-flat recline: the Bugaboo Butterfly 2 now offers this from birth (an upgrade on the original model), and the Silver Cross Jet 5 has a lie-flat recline with a built-in newborn nest. The Cybex Libelle, by contrast, only reclines to 30-40 degrees.

guide.q: Is the cheapest option good enough?
guide.a: For occasional travel, budget options like the Ickle Bubba Pisces (£119) or Joie Pact (£160) performed well in testing, though both need two hands to fold and have smaller storage. The pricier Maxi-Cosi Lara² was praised for feeling sturdy over rough terrain despite its mid-range price.

guide.q: How much storage will I actually get?
guide.a: Cabin-approved strollers generally sacrifice basket size for compactness. The Bugaboo Butterfly 2 and Cosatto Yo! both offer a relatively generous 8kg basket, the Maxi-Cosi Lara² has two smaller baskets, while the Silver Cross Jet 5's basket holds only up to 5kg and is front-access only.
